Save Table

sbf_save_table.Rd

Saves a data frame as .rds and .csv files with the unrounded values and as a .md file with the values rounded and formatted for display.

Usage

sbf_save_table(
  x,
  x_name = substitute(x),
  sub = sbf_get_sub(),
  main = sbf_get_main(),
  caption = "",
  report = TRUE,
  tag = "",
  notes = "",
  proportion = FALSE,
  format_column = list(),
  round_as_estimate = character(0),
  no_big_mark = character(0),
  drop_sd = FALSE
)

Arguments

x

The data frame to save.

x_name

A string of the name.

sub

A string or character vector specifying the path to the sub folder (by default the current sub folder).

main

A string specifying the path to the main folder (by default the current main folder)

caption

A string of the caption.

report

A flag specifying whether to include in a report.

tag

A string of the tag.

notes

A string of additional notes to save with the metadata.

proportion

A flag specifying whether the columns estimate, lower, upper and sd are proportions, in which case significant digits are counted from the nearer of 0 and 1 in the .md file. The sd must not exceed sd(c(0, 1)).

format_column

A list of two-sided formulas of the form column ~ fun(.) specifying how to round and format numeric columns other than estimate, lower, upper and sd in the .md file. The function can return a numeric vector, which is formatted without further rounding, or a character vector, which is used as is. The values in the .rds and .csv files are not altered.

round_as_estimate

A character vector of numeric columns, other than estimate, lower, upper, sd and svalue, to round in the .md file to the same number of decimal places as estimate in the same row (e.g. an observed value compared with the estimate). Rows with a missing estimate are formatted as data. If proportion = TRUE the columns must also be proportions.

no_big_mark

A character vector of numeric columns (e.g. year) to format without commas as thousands separators in the .md file.

drop_sd

A flag specifying whether to drop the sd column from the .md file after using it to round estimate, lower and upper. If TRUE there must be a numeric sd column. The .rds and .csv files retain the sd column.

Value

An invisible string of the path to the saved object.

Details

In the .md file, estimates are rounded following the rounding policy in the usepois report template, which is adapted from Cole (2015). The column estimate is rounded to the second significant digit of the column sd if present and otherwise of 1/4 of the interval between the columns lower and upper. The columns lower and upper are rounded to one fewer decimal place than the estimate but to at least two significant digits. Estimates without an sd or interval are rounded to three significant digits. The column svalue is rounded to one decimal place. Other double columns are rounded to four significant digits, without adding trailing zeros beyond the digits of the value, while integer columns are not rounded. Significant trailing zeros are retained, commas are used as thousands separators for numbers of 1000 or more except in the columns named by no_big_mark, and numeric columns are padded with spaces to align their decimal points. The .md file is not saved if getOption("sbf.save_md") is FALSE, in which case any existing .md file for the table is deleted.

References

Cole, T.J. 2015. Too many digits: the presentation of numerical data. Archives of Disease in Childhood 100(7): 608-609. doi:10.1136/archdischild-2014-307149 .

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
sbf_save_table(
  coef,
  caption = "Parameter estimates.",
  format_column = list(zscore ~ round(., 1))
)
sbf_save_table(ppc, round_as_estimate = "observed")
sbf_save_table(counts, no_big_mark = "year")
} # }
